body: The perf benchmarks are all okay and don't show a regression with this release, which means it's probably not a problem with the rules. This could have more to do with the changes to ignored files, but it's very hard to tell without having the your full directory to run through. I don't suppose you can share the code?

@nzakas 

> I don't suppose you can share the code?

Unfortunately it's semi-private. However, I didn't just upgrade grunt-eslint & change a bunch of unrelated files, when I noticed it works slower than before I swapped only ESLint from 0.6.0 to 0.5.1 via:

``` bash
cd node_modules/grunt-eslint
rm -rf node_modules/eslint
npm install eslint@0.5.1
```

and run `grunt eslint` again; that's where those times from the original report came from. So the only change was, in fact, a new ESLint version.

I don't doubt you're seeing a slowdown, it's just going to be hard to track down by anyone other than you since you're the only one who can do before/after comparisons. My theory is that it's related to directory traversal and how ignored files and/or config file resolution work, as those changed in 0.6.0. 

I'll leave this open if you or someone else want to investigate. Unfortunately, without a repro case, I can't spend too much time on it vs. the other open issues.
I run a git bisect on it and the regression was introduced in bfef646d864f892b51d53d88d8b6339671b55ff9.

More specifically, removing these lines:
https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/514e398b374194e3aef643c9516ed627db93f2a5/lib/cli.js#L182-L191
restores previous performance.

Upon further investigation: the `cacheExclusions` method was taking all that time when it was caching the `node_modules/**` part. Changing it to `node_modules` fixed the issue.

I don't know if there's anything left to do here, then. If you think it's worth it, you might want to recognize `path/**` as `path` and not resolve the `**` since it's equivalent in ESLint. People often write this pattern since some tools can't deal with directories but just files so it might be common enough.

Your decision!

Hm, it seems this issue is valid. If I pass exactly the same files to jsHint and ESLint with the same `.eslintignore` and `.jshintignore`, I have this perf problem. Both files contain the `node_modules/**`, `vendor/**` and similar entries and yet it doesn't slow down jsHint but only ESLint.

Unfortunately, if `test/vendor` is in `.eslintignore` and I pass `test/**/*.js` to ESLint, it doesn't ignore the `vendor` subdirectory.

Passing individual files is important for development since linting all files after each change would be unacceptably slow and solutions like `grunt-newer` require dealing with files, not directories. Perhaps sth could be done to improve performance here?

Again, please don't take my comments for saying your report was invalid. I believed you were seeing a performance issue from the start, I just had no way of verifying it and therefore no way to verify if something I did could fix it.

I'm planning on ripping apart how we do exclusions, so I'll leave this issue open to see if my planned changes improve the situation at all.

> Again, please don't take my comments for saying your report was invalid.

Sure; I was replying to my own remark in an earlier commit. I tried to narrow the issue down as much as possible, especially that you don't have access to my code.

I changed `.eslintignore` to use `dir/**` for all excluded directories except `node_modules` which I don't pass to the Grunt task. A little duct type but works for now.

I'll re-test it once the refactor lands.
As @nzakas said, the exclusions seem ripe for an overhaul. I _may_ have fixed this issue in another bug fix here: #839. @mzgol could you try checking out that branch and see if it helps?
@spadgos With your PR it's taking even longer... 3.4s on `master` with `node_modules` in `.eslintignore` and when I change it to `node_modules/**` it's 5.6s on `master` and 7.6s on your branch.
Okay, I did a refactor this morning. Can you check out the `ignored` branch here and let me know if you see difference?

issue.body:
There are a number of issues already open around how ignored files work (or don't work). They are:
- [x] Performance problems (#901 and #814)
- [x] Files in ignored directories still linted when specified on command line (#837)
- [x] ESLint can't pass files and directories at the same time (#853)

We've also patched ignored files a bunch in the last release.

It's become clear to me that there's a problem with the way the ignored file functionality is implemented at a fundamental level. It's time to refactor and clean this mess up.

body:
@nzakas In the `ignored` branch `.eslintignore` files are not ignored. I have the `test/.eslintignore` file containing:

```
unit/vendor/**
**/*.defs.js
templates.js
```

and yet I get errors for files under `test/unit/vendor/**`.

I guess it may be caused by the fact that I have the ignore file at `test/.eslintignore` and rules files at `test/unit/.eslintrc` and `test/e2e/.eslintrc`.

EDIT: no, that's not it. In `app/` I have both `.eslintignore` & `.eslintrc` and yet, although I have `vendor/**` in `app/.eslintignore`, files in `app/vendor/**` are checked.

Okay, I know what happened. It looks like we were doing cascading ignore files, so you could have them all up and down the source tree. My change only looks for `.eslintignore` in the current working directory. 

The cascading was never the way I intended this functionality to work, (JSHint also supports just the root directory), but it snuck in somehow. Can you try creating a top-level `.eslintignore` with your settings and see what happens?

What do you mean by "current working directory" here? If I have a `.jshintignore` containing `node_modules/**` and I do:

``` js
cd mode_modules/lodash
jshint lodash.js
```

I don't get any errors so exclusion still works here.
